title: Human RNA polymerase III termination favors decomposition over facilitated recycling
task: Characterize mechanistic pathways of RNA polymerase III transcription termination
key_results: Identified three-way mechanistic trifurcation: decomposing termination (dominant), recycling termination (2-14%), and readthrough
T-tracts of ≥4 consecutive thymidines required for robust termination; longer tracts favor recycling over decomposition
comments: The single-molecule resolution elegantly resolves pathway heterogeneity, though the physiological significance of the 2-14% recycling fraction relative to bacterial systems remains to be established in vivo.

model_io.model: Human RNA polymerase III intrinsic termination
inputs: DNA template with T-tract and upstream hairpin
outputs: Dissociation kinetics of RNA and DNA

hypotheses.hypothesis: Decomposing termination (simultaneous RNA-DNA dissociation) dominates human RNAP3 unlike bacterial systems where recycling prevails
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; decomposing accounts for 86-98% of termination events

hypotheses.hypothesis: Longer T-tracts promote recycling relative to decomposing termination
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; longer tracts increase recycling pathway probability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Upstream RNA hairpins enhance overall termination efficiency with distance-dependent effects
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; hairpin impact decreases with distance from T-tract, affecting both pathways similarly
